sections.html:
Probate in Kansas runs through the district court. Its job is to prove a will, name someone to manage the estate, pay valid debts and pass what is left to the people entitled to it. Every probate proceeding is under the district court's authority, and juries are not used.

If the person left a will, it names an executor. With no will, the court appoints an administrator. Either one is personally responsible for handling the estate properly: notifying heirs and creditors, inventorying and protecting the assets, paying taxes and valid claims, and distributing the rest. Appointing an executor usually takes four to five weeks from the day the petition is filed, though no two estates run on the same schedule.

For someone who inherited a house, the practical point is simple. Until a personal representative has been appointed, nobody has clear authority to sign a sale contract for the estate. A person who deals with the dead owner's property without a formal court appointment can be held personally responsible for what they do.

Four dates matter most to a family thinking about selling an inherited house: the six-month window to file a will, the 30-day publication step, the four-month creditor period and the small estate ceiling of $75,000.

Main Kansas probate time limits and thresholds
StepRule
Filing a will for probate (K.S.A. 59-617)A will does not pass property unless a petition is filed within six months of the death
Publishing notice to creditors (K.S.A. 59-709)Petitioner gives notice within 30 days after filing, once a week for three consecutive weeks, in a county newspaper
Creditor claim window (K.S.A. 59-2239)Four months from first publication, or 30 days after actual notice to a known creditor if that is later
Small estate affidavit (K.S.A. 59-1507b)Personal property can move without letters when probate assets are $75,000 or less
Earliest closingAn estate with assets beyond allowances and debts cannot close before six months after death

The 30-day publication period is recent. A 2024 law (Senate Bill 379) lengthened it from 10 days to 30 days after the petition is filed, so older articles and forms may still show the shorter number.

Only property titled in the dead person's name alone, with no beneficiary or survivor rights attached, normally goes through probate. Several kinds of property bypass it:

  • Property held in joint tenancy with right of survivorship
  • Life insurance paid to a named beneficiary other than the estate
  • Bank accounts with a pay on death designation
  • Assets with transfer on death provisions, including securities, titled vehicles and real estate

The last item matters for houses. If the owner recorded a transfer on death deed before dying, the house passes to the named beneficiary outside the estate. Our guide to the Kansas transfer on death deed covers how those deeds work. If no such deed or survivorship title exists, the house is a probate asset.

Yes, an executor can sell, and the route depends on the will. Under K.S.A. 59-1413, if a will authorizes the executor to sell property, the executor may use that power without an order of the district court, unless the will provides otherwise. The power cannot be used while a proceeding to contest the will or to probate a later will is pending.

A buyer in good faith who takes title under that power gets the real estate free of the creditors' liens and claims against the estate and the heirs. Those claims move to the sale proceeds. Tax liens are the exception, and the statute says the transfer does not affect them.

When the will gives no power of sale, or there is no will, the administrator petitions the court instead. K.S.A. 59-2303 lets the petition name a prospective purchaser and the proposed terms, ask the court to approve appraisers and ask it to confirm the deal. If the buyer is related to the fiduciary by blood or finances, the petition has to say so. If there is no relationship, the petition says that instead.

The court path also has a public auction option. Notice of an auction of real estate must run once a week for three consecutive weeks in a county newspaper, and the sale date falls no sooner than 10 days and no later than 30 days after the last publication (K.S.A. 59-2308). Many families prefer a negotiated private sale for that reason.

sections.h2: What a small estate affidavit covers
sections.html:
The small estate affidavit in K.S.A. 59-1507b covers personal property only, so it does not move title to a house. When a Kansas resident dies with probate assets of $75,000 or less, a successor can give a bank or other holder an affidavit and collect personal property without letters of administration. The 2024 amendment also lets the property go to a person claiming to be a successor, or as that successor directs.

Real estate needs a different step. When someone dies without a will and leaves only real estate, a determination of descent proceeding can be started any time six months after death, and it typically takes about 30 days. That proceeding gives the heirs a court record of who owns the house before they sell.

The Kansas courts run a self-help probate page that links the Judicial Council forms, including the small estates affidavit. Questions go to the local district court.

sections.h2: Costs and taxes on a Kansas estate
sections.html:
Fees for the executor and the lawyer are not fixed by law. They must reflect the fair value of the work compared with the size of the estate, and the probate court approves them. Court fees are set by law, and publication charges and a bond premium may be added.

Property tax keeps running while the estate is open. Kansas real estate tax is due in full by December 20, or in two halves, with the second half due May 10 of the next year (K.S.A. 79-2004). Unpaid amounts draw interest at the statutory rate plus five percentage points. A house that sits through a long probate can pick up a tax bill and interest before anyone sells it. Our Kansas property tax guide walks through the calendar.

A transfer on death deed does not avoid creditors. An executor should not prepare the estate's tax returns without a lawyer's help.

sections.h2: First steps for heirs who inherit a house
sections.html:
Protect the house, call a probate lawyer and gather the paperwork, in that order. Nothing should be done to disturb the dead person's property unless it is needed to keep it from being lost or destroyed. Contact a lawyer soon after the death, with the will in hand at the first meeting.

  • Locate the original will and note the date of death, since the six-month filing window starts there.
  • Find the recorded deed. Check whether it shows joint tenants or a transfer on death beneficiary.
  • List the mortgage, tax and utility accounts, and note the next property tax due date.
  • Ask the lawyer whether the will gives the executor a power of sale, since that changes whether a court order is needed.
  • Decide among the heirs who will sign, because every owner or the court-appointed representative must agree to a sale.

A cash purchase fits at the point where the personal representative has authority, and the sale proceeds then pass through the estate account to creditors and heirs. A cash buyer can close without waiting on a bank's loan approval, which removes one source of delay in an estate that already has court steps to finish.

We buy houses as-is, so an inherited property that needs repairs, has personal belongings left in it or sits vacant can still be considered. The title company handling the closing will want to see the court's appointment of the executor or administrator and, where the will grants no power of sale, the court's order. Ask the estate's lawyer which documents apply to your file before you sign anything.

faqs.q: How long does probate take in Kansas?
faqs.a: There is no fixed length. Appointing an executor usually takes four to five weeks after filing, creditors have four months, and an estate with assets beyond allowances and debts cannot close before six months after the date of death. Many estates run longer.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited house in Kansas before probate is finished?
faqs.a: Sometimes. If the will gives the executor a power of sale, no court order is needed under K.S.A. 59-1413. Without that power, the administrator asks the district court for approval under K.S.A. 59-2303. Either way a court-appointed representative must exist first.

faqs.q: Does a small estate affidavit transfer a house in Kansas?
faqs.a: No. K.S.A. 59-1507b covers personal property when probate assets are $75,000 or less. Real estate needs probate or a determination of descent, unless a transfer on death deed or survivorship title already controls it.

faqs.q: How many days does a creditor have to file a claim?
faqs.a: Four months from the first publication of notice, or 30 days after actual notice to a known or reasonably ascertainable creditor if that is later (K.S.A. 59-2239). Claims presented after that are barred.

faqs.q: Do I need a lawyer for a Kansas probate?
faqs.a: Not every estate requires one, but it is wise to contact a lawyer soon after a death, and an executor should not prepare tax returns without a lawyer's guidance. This page is general information and not legal advice.
